sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Westlake, Ohio?
sections.html:
Westlake is a Cuyahoga County suburb about 12 miles west of downtown Cleveland. It covers 15.93 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau estimates 33,904 residents on July 1, 2025, a 1.0% drop from the 2020 estimates base. City Hall is at 27700 Hilliard Boulevard and answers at 440-871-3300 from 8 am to 4 pm.

For permits and property maintenance, ask City Hall directly. For deeds and value complaints, use the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office and Board of Revision. The sections below explain what each office does and what the numbers say about the market.

sections.h2: How did Dover Township become Westlake?
sections.html:
European settlers first arrived on October 10, 1810, when the area belonged to Dover Township. Bay Village split off in 1901, and a southern piece joined North Olmsted in 1912. The remaining residents formed Dover Village in 1913. The name changed to Westlake in 1940 to avoid confusion with Dover in Tuscarawas County, and Westlake became a city in 1957.

Growth came fast after that. Population rose from 4,912 in 1950 to 12,906 in 1960 and to 27,018 by 1990, then settled near 34,000. The 2020 census counted 15,508 housing units in the city, 5.7% of them vacant.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about owning in Westlake?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 show an older, mostly owner-occupied suburb.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 73.1%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $368,200.
  • Median monthly owner costs: $2,071 with a mortgage and $926 without one.
  • Median gross rent: $1,570.
  • Households: 14,424, at 2.29 people per household.
  • Median household income: $112,200; 60.2% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.
  • Residents 65 and older: 25.1%, with a 2020 census median age of 47.4.

One in four residents is 65 or older, so many sales here involve owners downsizing or heirs settling an estate. Foreign-born residents make up 12.6% of the population, and 15.2% of residents age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home.

sections.h2: Which employers and shopping districts support Westlake home values?
sections.html:
Westlake is a headquarters town. Nordson, American Greetings, Hyland Software, Scott Fetzer, TravelCenters of America and Equity Trust are all based here. The city's 2021 financial report lists University Hospitals Health System as the top employer at 3,202 workers, followed by Hyland Software at 1,987 and American Greetings at 1,167.

Crocker Park, a mixed-use center built around a small-town street plan, holds 1,050,000 square feet of retail, 650 residential units and 100,000 square feet of office space. Mean travel time to work for Westlake residents is 24.4 minutes, and the city sits 12 miles from downtown Cleveland.

sections.h2: How does a deed move through the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office?
sections.html:
The Fiscal Office's Transfer and Recording division combines the old auditor, recorder and engineer functions. It sits at 2079 E. Ninth Street, 4th floor, Cleveland, and answers at 216-443-2060. Office hours are Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and recording runs from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

  • Every transfer needs either a DTE 100 Statement of Value and Receipt or a DTE 100-EX statement of the reason for an exemption from the conveyance fee.
  • The standard recording fee rose to $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after that on October 24, 2024, under Ohio Senate Bill 94.
  • County staff cannot give legal advice, and the county describes preparing a deed as the practice of law. The seller may act as their own attorney.
  • Electronic recording is available through registration, and a property fraud notification service is offered.
  • Heirs can use the county's Great Estates Program pages, which explain how to avoid unnecessary costs and delays in settling an estate.

sections.h2: When can you dispute your Westlake property value?
sections.html:
The Cuyahoga County Board of Revision hears complaints against the valuation of real property under Ohio Revised Code Chapter 5715. For tax year 2025 the filing period closed, and the window for tax year 2026 runs from January 1, 2027 through March 31, 2027. The statute sets the deadline at March 31 of the year after the tax year, or the first-half collection close if later.

The board sits at 2079 East Ninth Street, Second Floor, answers at 216-443-7195 and takes email at BORInfo@cuyahogacounty.gov. Its site offers state-prescribed forms, a search of closed and pending complaints from 2018 forward, and evidence guidance. Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 requires a complainant to give the board all information or evidence they hold that affects the property.

Read the evidence guidance on the board's site before you file, since a complainant who withholds evidence can be barred from using it on appeal.

sections.h2: What does Ohio require of a Westlake seller?
sections.html:
Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 requires the seller of a one-to-four unit home to complete the state property disclosure form and deliver a signed copy. Several transfers are exempt, including those by a fiduciary in an estate, guardianship or trust, transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, and transfers to a buyer who has lived in the house for a year or more.

If the buyer gets the form after signing, the buyer can rescind in writing within three business days of receiving it. That risk is easy to avoid by handing over the form with the first offer.

sections.h2: How do your options compare for a quick Westlake sale?
sections.html:
A median owner-occupied value of $368,200 means a Westlake listing reaches buyers who finance with mortgages, and the timeline depends on their lender. A direct purchase of the house as-is can close on a date you choose, usually at a price that accounts for repairs.

  • Put every offer in writing, with the closing date, who pays closing costs and whether repairs are excluded.
  • Request proof of funds from any cash buyer before you sign.
  • Compare the net amount after payoff of any mortgage and unpaid property tax, not the headline price.

sections.h2: What should you ask City Hall before listing a Westlake house?
sections.html:
The city's Codified Ordinances are published on American Legal Publishing, and the posted version is current through July 16, 2026. Rather than guess at local rules, ask City Hall the same short list of questions every time.

  • Is there an open permit, or one that never received a final inspection?
  • If the house is a rental, does the city require a license or registration, and does it pass to a new owner?
  • Are there any open property maintenance or zoning complaints?
  • Which sewer and water accounts need a final reading at closing?

Write down each answer with the date and the name of the department. A buyer's title company will ask for the same answers.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Cuyahoga County?
faqs.a: The standard recording fee is $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each extra page since October 24, 2024. The Fiscal Office also requires a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX form with every transfer. Call 216-443-2060 to confirm.

faqs.q: When is the deadline for a Westlake property value complaint?
faqs.a: March 31 of the year after the tax year. The Board of Revision lists January 1 through March 31, 2027 as the window for tax year 2026. Call 216-443-7195 with questions.

faqs.q: Does the county require a rental disclosure in Westlake?
faqs.a: Yes. The Fiscal Office says Ohio Revised Code 5323.02 and 5323.99 require an owner of residential rental property to file information with the county fiscal officer.
27700 Hilliard Blvd, Westlake, OH 44145. The main number is 440-871-3300, and hours are 8 am to 4 pm.

faqs.q: Do I need the Ohio disclosure form if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: Often no. Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 excuses a seller who inherited the property and has not lived in it within the past year, and it excuses fiduciaries acting for an estate.
